chunks: The camel driver and the mule driver, when the journey presses on them in earnest, should shorten the salat (prayer) between the two stopping places, and they should perform it complete in the two stopping places.

key_terms.أَتَمَّا: they performed the salat (prayer) in full
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: the mule driver or hired transport driver
key_terms.اَلسَّيْرُ: traveling or movement on the journey
key_terms.اَلْمَنْزِلَيْنِ: the two stopping places or stations on the route

ai.seo_question: When should a camel driver or mule driver shorten or complete salat (prayer) during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about travelers whose work involves continual movement, such as camel drivers and mule drivers. It states that they shorten their salat (prayer) while actively traveling between stopping places, but perform the full salat (prayer) when they are at those stopping places.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1278 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"The camel driver (al-Jammal) and the mule driver (al-Mukari) should shorten their prayers while traveling between their stopping places, but when they reach their stopping places, they should offer the complete prayers”.
